  "markdown_report": "Select a dependency-isolated, mutation-tested BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter as the first experiment. At 0% progress, reliable measurements provide a foundation for testing training interventions; diagnostic improvements alone do not establish ranking gains.

**Insights from supplied evidence.** (1) All four recent sampler and exported-serving checks passed before missing-SciPy failures. This establishes diagnostic execution failure without establishing a serving defect; agreement alone also cannot establish semantic correctness. (2) Recent-item deletion reduced target scores across categories, with Electronics diagnostic hit@10 decreasing by 0.125. These training-prefix effects motivate recency hypotheses without demonstrating validation gains. (3) Residual probes reported stale prerequisite failures. Availability and gate reasons must derive from current execution state, retaining completed measurements.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Recommender metamorphic testing [1] supports input/output relations without exact recommendation labels, but its classical-library results require BERT4Rec validation. (2) Mutation assessment [2] concerns industrial optimisation software; effectiveness depends on relations, faults and inputs. Surviving sampled tests does not prove equivalence. (3) BERT4Rec [3] supplies independent masking, position and readout semantics. Shared preprocessing bugs can survive training/export parity checks.

The framework groups research into three directions: execution reliability, semantic correctness, and behavioral usefulness.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension |
|---|---|---|
| Execution | Dependency failure; stale gate reasons | Independent outcomes with verified rollback |
| Correctness | Passing checkpoint/serving parity | Independent semantic fixtures and controlled faults |
| Behavior | Recent-deletion effects | Budgeted, serving-aligned audits |

Three atomic ideas follow; scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten. Difficulty increases with complexity.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isolate probe execution | 2/7/3 | O: precise adaptation; P: preserves evidence; D: small core wrapper | O: standard practice; P: indirect ranking benefit; D: state restoration needs care |
| Mutation-test semantic fixtures [1–3] | 4/7/6 | O: family-specific combination; P: reusable assurance; D: bounded fixtures | O: established technique; P: incomplete fault coverage; D: independent oracles and rollback are substantial |
| Audit terminal/reconstruction boundary gradients | 5/6/6 | O: specific ranking adaptation; P: objective hypotheses; D: reuses autograd | O: established ingredients; P: local evidence only; D: tied-gradient accounting |

Choose the first two as one diagnostic reliability experiment. Defer gradient audits until measurement reliability passes; no supplied evidence justifies a new training mechanism yet.

```text
snapshot mutable state; use separate deterministic diagnostic batches
run probes independently; retain measurements and definitions
derive gates from current sampler/parity outcomes
run manually specified clean fixtures and one reversible fault at a time
record intended-assertion kills, survivors, coverage and runtime
verify rollback before continuing; stop on rollback failure
restore parameters, owned hooks, module modes and RNG state
```

Fixtures cover left-padded readout, appended MASK, padding exclusion, reserved-candidate filtering and all four routes. Calibrate numerical tolerances against repeat-run noise; score/rank changes alone do not establish semantic faults. Freeze fixtures before mutation assessment and disclose later revisions to limit test-suite overfitting.

Preserve every adapter interface, one trained checkpoint/category, routing, predictor consistency, seeds, training limits, paths and host evaluation. Charge diagnostics to the shared budget. Keep qualitative abstentions separate from rejection; unavailable compatibility evidence remains unknown.",
  "idea": {
    "description": "Build a dependency-isolated, mutation-tested diagnostic adapter for the corrected BERT4Rec baseline. Preserve completed measurements after optional-probe failures, verify rollback, and assess semantic probes using independent fixtures and temporary controlled faults.",
    "motivation": "Recent supplied results show successful sampler and serialized-serving parity checks followed by missing-SciPy failures in every category, while residual availability reasons contradict successful prerequisites. Reliable execution records and independent semantic oracles are a feasible early-stage priority. They support subsequent experiments but do not demonstrate better recommendations. Retain terminal/reconstruction allocation and ranking-boundary gradient audits as later hypotheses rather than adding an unsupported training change now.",
    "implementation_notes": "Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), the actual view.model, and every supplied ModelView interface: item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Keep family-specific sample_batch and B x L loader tensors compatible. Propagate the actual category explicitly from the training loop. Return metrics and metric_definitions with per-probe status, attempted/completed counts, elapsed time and precise reasons. Unavailable measurements are null, never zero. Preserve existing embedding, masked-margin and valid behavioral probes; unavailable item-category breakdown lists remain empty. A mapped embedding-cosine value near 0.5 does not establish representation quality or convergence.

Keep completed metrics and definitions in an outer accumulator. Isolate optional imports inside their dependent probes. Distinguish prerequisite failure, unsupported architecture, execution failure and rollback failure. Recompute behavioral and residual gate reasons from current sampler/parity outcomes; report the actual optional-dependency error when prerequisites passed. Replace an optional dependency only with a mathematically equivalent implementation checked against independently calculated small fixtures; otherwise mark the dependent probe unavailable. Test missing dependencies with a scoped targeted import mock or patch.dict(sys.modules, {'scipy': None}); account for cached references at their use sites. Assert that prior measurements survive, later independent probes execute after successful cleanup, and no stale gate reason appears. Failure injection is a proposed test, not an observed result.

Use independent expected values instead of importing production preprocessing or readout helpers. For width six and history [a,b], expect [0,0,0,a,b,MASK] and readout index 5; count_nonzero-1 incorrectly selects index 2. Inject distinct position-coded hidden states to expose wrong gathering, and capture actual encoder inputs to detect omitted MASK. Cover singleton, partially padded, full-capacity and over-capacity histories; truncate to the latest maxlen-1 interactions before appending MASK. Assert exact token/index expectations, valid real supervised IDs and MASK at every supervised position. Training-input checks cannot establish the sampler's entire prefix provenance from tensors alone; fixtures must exercise the actual family-specific constructor with known training histories. Repeated earlier target IDs may remain legitimate history. Never introduce shifted prediction targets into bidirectional input.

Check padding exclusion by perturbing only representations at positions already masked as PAD, with identical token masks, real-token positions, weights and position IDs. Force nonzero PAD representations through a scoped test hook so disabling exclusion has an observable effect. Check real-position outputs, including the appended MASK. Do not assume invariance after arbitrary padding shifts with learned absolute positions. Separately force PAD/MASK logits highest through a diagnostic hook and assert neither reserved token appears in recommendations. Test score permutation equivariance for candidates, and batch permutation equivariance, with independently specified expectations.

Exercise every category route using distinct synthetic checkpoint fingerprints, overlapping local item IDs and independently specified outputs. Reorder and interleave category requests to expose routing/cache faults. Synthetic fixtures are untrained diagnostic artifacts; they do not supply recommendation scores to the deployed system. Test wrong routing and altered checkpoint state separately. Use the actual exported loader and embedded predictor writer. Compare current-model and freshly loaded current-category checkpoint states exactly, including tensor shapes and dtypes, then compare finite evaluation-mode FP32 scores on short, full-length, truncated and batched histories. Avoid runtime source reconstruction. Agreement cannot substitute for the independent semantic fixtures.

Preserve existing serving-parity tolerances atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 for continuity. For new deterministic semantic fixtures, preregister proposed atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5 and record repeat-run noise before fault assessment. If the proposed fixture thresholds are unsupported on the actual backend, report the issue and freeze a documented revision before assessment. Token, index, route and checkpoint-state checks remain exact. Construct deliberate mutant effects comfortably above numerical uncertainty; compare ordered rankings only where score gaps exceed that uncertainty. Exact checkpoint mismatch remains a state-identity failure even when sampled scores agree. A changed model need not change every ranking.

Freeze clean fixtures, applicability conditions, mutation operators, intended assertions and numerical thresholds before running the mutation assessment. Inject one fault at a time: count-minus-one readout, omitted inference MASK, disabled PAD exclusion, reserved-candidate leakage, wrong category route and corrupted checkpoint state. Instrument the changed path and verify that each fixture makes its effect observable. A kill requires failure of the intended semantic assertion, not any exception or an unrelated assertion. Report killed, surviving, unexercised and invalid/proven-equivalent mutants separately, with reasons. Do not label a survivor equivalent merely because sampled tests passed. Report per-fault counts and, where meaningful, detection among exercised valid non-equivalent mutants; list unresolved-equivalence survivors explicitly. Report clean-control assertion failures and confirmed false alarms separately. Clean controls include the unchanged network and benign candidate/request permutations. These finite, designed mutants measure coverage of specified faults, not a general fault-detection probability. Hold back additional fixture histories or fault variants for a later fixed assessment; label probe revisions after inspection exploratory.

Make restoration local to every probe and every fault, not only to run_full_diagnosis. Register cleanup immediately after each modification using try/finally or ExitStack. Clone state_dict tensor values rather than retaining its tensor references; separately snapshot touched nonpersistent buffers, mutable attributes, gradients and requires_grad flags. Restore tensor contents under torch.no_grad() without replacing Parameter objects, preserving tied parameters and optimizer references. Save and restore every module's training flag individually, including mixed train/eval states. Remove only hooks installed by the probe through their handles; always_call=True is not a substitute for cleanup. Restore Python, NumPy, Torch CPU/CUDA RNG states and all explicit generators touched. Verify restored tensors, modes, flags, gradients and generator states before continuing. A rollback failure stops further probes and marks their results unavailable; it must not permit contaminated measurements or training to continue. Never save or deploy a temporary mutant.

Use a separate deterministic diagnostic loader with its own generator and num_workers=0, or cached cloned diagnostic batches. Do not consume the active training iterator. Saving a loader generator does not rewind consumed batches, worker RNG or prefetch queues; capture required states before iterator construction. torch.random.fork_rng covers Torch state only, so handle other RNGs separately. Record diagnostic batch identities or hashes and configuration so fixtures are reproducible.

Before execution, serialize fixture histories, valid IDs, route fingerprints, mutation operators, expected assertions, dependency-failure injections, loader settings, tolerances, software/backend versions, diagnostic cap and stopping rules. Preserve raw outcomes, state-restoration checks, availability and per-probe costs. CUDA-synchronize timing boundaries where appropriate. Charge diagnostics, debugging and failures to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No runtime or detection rate is claimed before measurement. Derive interpretation prompts from measured values, definitions, controls and availability. Separate execution failure, semantic failure, training-prefix sensitivity and host validation; neither fewer metamorphic violations nor larger training margins establish higher HR@10.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts remain beneath the trial directory and execution single-GPU. Preserve the supplied corrected baseline architecture, sampler, optimizer and host checkpoint/evaluation cadence during this diagnostic experiment. Each category deploys exactly one independently trained, unmutated BERT4Rec checkpoint; no independent predictors, score fusion, averaging or extra fitted experts. Preserve reserved-mask supervision and appended-mask inference using the actual final nonpadding position, never count-1. Keep checkpoint configuration and predictor writer synchronized; diagnostic-only hooks must never enter serving.

Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users/category. Use only public interaction histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Ratings, review content, item categories/prices/stores, ownership, compatibility specifications and simulator traits remain unobserved unless directly evidenced by allowed content. Separate choose-now, deferred relevance, explicit mismatch and cannot-identify judgments as exploratory qualitative observations, without treating abstentions as negative labels or sparse feedback as population preferences. Selection remains unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10, with the supplied splits and candidates; never read hidden tests, modify evaluation, reuse other trials' checkpoints or assert unmeasured gains.",
    "pseudocode": "class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Independent diagnostic batches; do not advance the training iterator.
        protocol = load_frozen_trial_local_protocol()
        batches = obtain_separate_seeded_or_cached_cloned_batches(protocol)
        metrics, definitions = {}, {}
        outer_snapshot = snapshot_all_touched_state()
        try:
            for probe in prerequisite_and_descriptive_probes:
                outcome = execute_probe_with_verified_rollback(probe, batches)
                accumulate(metrics, definitions, outcome)
                if outcome.rollback_failed:
                    mark_remaining_probes_unavailable('rollback failure')
                    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

            for probe in behavioral_and_optional_probes:
                gate = evaluate_current_prerequisites(probe, metrics)
                if not gate.passed:
                    accumulate_unavailable(probe, gate.actual_reasons)
                    continue
                outcome = execute_probe_with_verified_rollback(probe, batches)
                accumulate(metrics, definitions, outcome)
                if outcome.rollback_failed:
                    mark_remaining_probes_unavailable('rollback failure')
                    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

            if within_preregistered_diagnostic_cap():
                run_independently_specified_clean_fixtures()
                for fault in protocol.semantic_faults:
                    with verified_reversible_fault(fault):
                        exercised = instrument_changed_path_and_observability()
                        result = run_frozen_independent_assertions(fault)
                        record_mutant_state_and_intended_assertion_result(
                            exercised, result)
                    # Context exit verifies rollback before the next fault.
                run_scoped_optional_dependency_failure_fixtures()
                assert_completed_metrics_survive_and_later_probes_execute()

            return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
        finally:
            remove_only_owned_hooks()
            restore_and_verify_touched_state(outer_snapshot)
            # Restoration failure is fatal to further diagnostic/training work.

# execute_probe_with_verified_rollback snapshots tensors, touched attributes,
# buffers, gradients, requires_grad flags, every module mode, all RNGs and
# explicit generators. It captures a probe exception only after rollback succeeds.
# It records unavailable/error distinctly and preserves outer accumulated results.

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt_containing_measured_values_definitions_and_failure_reasons(
        raw_diagnosis,
        distinguish_execution_semantic_and_rollback_failures=True,
        distinguish_training_prefix_metrics_from_host_validation=True,
        prohibit_unmeasured_validation_and_user_trait_claims=True)

# Preserve baseline training, four routes and synchronized predictor writing.
# Deploy exactly one unmutated BERT4Rec checkpoint per category.",
